import.title: Import original assets
import.text: If you own Master of Orion (1993), pick its .LBX files (or the whole game folder). They are converted to PNG and JSON inside your browser and stored only on this device: nothing is uploaded.
The Classic theme then shows the original planet pictures and race portraits. The game is fully playable without them.
mods.title: Mods
mods.text: A mod is a folder with any of: mod.json (name, description, base theme), text/en.json (replaces any text of the game), rules.json (game numbers and ship designs) and images/*.png (for example images/site/terran.png, images/army.png, images/race/0.png, images/map/background.png).
See docs/MODDING.md in the repository for the full list.

help.lines: Grow your empire from a single planet. Every colony splits its production between five sliders: SHIP builds the selected design, DEFENSE builds missile bases and shields, INDUSTRY builds factories, ECOLOGY cleans pollution, terraforms and grows population, TECHNOLOGY funds research.
Select your colony ship in orbit, press Send fleet and click a planet inside the dashed range circles. Colony ships settle automatically on arrival; better colony bases settle hostile planets.

Research: choose one technology per field. Planetology unlocks hostile planets and terraforming, Propulsion range, engines and stargates, Construction cheaper factories and armor, Computers robotic controls and battle computers, Weapons and Force Fields everything for combat. Higher levels make ship parts cheaper and smaller.
Ships: design up to six ship classes from hulls, weapons, computers, shields, armor, engines and specials. Replacing or scrapping a design scraps its ships.
To conquer a planet, win the battle in its orbit (destroying its missile bases), then send transports from a nearby colony. Ships holding an enemy orbit bomb it (see Planets to turn this off).

Battles: when your ships or planets meet an enemy, the battle is fought on a grid. Stacks act in order of initiative: click a lit square to move, an enemy in a red frame to fire. Missiles take turns to arrive and can be dodged; asteroids block shots. Specials like stasis fields and pulsars have their own button. Let the computer fight if you prefer.
Nebulae block shields and halve speed. Stargates between your planets move fleets in one turn. The Guardian protects Orion: destroying it reveals its ancient technologies.

Races: meet other empires when your colonies come within fuel range of theirs. Ask for an audience to propose pacts, alliances, peace and trade, to threaten, to offer tribute or to exchange technology. Their mood and how much they trust you decide the answer; allies share fuel range and never fight.

Spies: give a budget per empire, then send them to steal technology or to sabotage factories, missile bases or stir up revolt. Security catches enemy spies. Taxes (Planets) fill the reserve, which you can send to any colony.
Random events strike: plagues, novas, comets, pirates, monsters, rebellions. Land troops on a rebel colony to restore order.

Win by eliminating every rival, or by being elected High Master by two thirds of the votes of the Galactic Council, which meets every 25 years once two thirds of the planets are settled. Refusing its verdict means war against everyone.
